A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same five-axis framework and Two-Gate guardrail. All 24 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figures 1–2 report original simulations of representational expansion and algorithmic training. Appendix 17 describes the synthetic data, policies, and experimental settings.

after.justification: V2 removes both experimental figures, the numerical findings in Section 9, and Appendix 17. The remaining main text and appendices contain theory and discussion, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The proof-triggered modification framework, Two-Gate validation and capacity conditions, and step-mass stopping mechanism remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of finite evidence and candidate selection do not establish a different procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic binary classification with Gaussian inputs, logistic labels, feature noise, and label flips. V2 removes this entire empirical coverage, including its representational and algorithmic evaluations, without adding another dataset or task.

E2.justification: Both reported TwoGate-versus-Destructive comparisons in Figures 1–2 are removed, leaving no evaluated comparator in v2. The additional policy variants named in v1 Appendix 17 are not separately identified in the plotted results.

E3.justification: The experimental protocols disappear: fixed train/validation/test splits, evaluation of the last accepted predictor using test 0–1 loss, and generalization-gap tracking during continued training. The polynomial-degree sweep and 50,000-iteration training setting are removed with their experiments.

E4.justification: V2 deletes the polynomial-degree sensitivity study in Figure 1 and the step-mass/generalization-gap trajectory in Figure 2. These examined how increasing complexity or continued training affects generalization under guarded and destructive policies.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3's reporting of five and twenty seeds, respectively, and Figure 2's shaded variability display are removed. V2 retains theoretical probability bounds but provides no empirical run-count or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All experimental curves and their qualitative findings are removed. Section 9 also loses its reported test-loss comparison of 0.409 versus 0.350; these textual values should not be conflated with Figure 1's displayed values. V2 supplies no replacement empirical results.

T1.justification: Section 4 now distinguishes reasonable utilities from the stronger capacity-bonus subclass required for destruction results, and Section 3 explicitly defines distribution-free and computable PAC learning. The principal bounds and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged; Appendices 12–13 still retain the earlier bonus-requiring definition.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the abstract's claim of numerical validation and adds an Axis clarity contribution identifying algorithmic self-modification as a subset of online learning. The central capacity-boundary and Two-Gate claims remain, with the substrate contribution additionally acknowledging computability.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an explanation of overfitting through evidence-based selection among update rules. Section 3 drops the claim that capacity certification can be performed axis by axis, and Section 9 removes the assertion of exponential compounding while retaining the global-capacity warning.

D1.justification: Deleting Appendix 17 removes the data-generation instructions and implementation settings, including noise and label-flip levels, regularization, learning rate, batch size, and the 2.5 step-mass budget. These experimental reproduction details are not relocated elsewhere in v2.

R1.justification: V2 removes the Section 3 discussion and references to Self-Refine, Reflexion, Voyager, and Tree of Thoughts. It also explicitly positions the algorithmic axis within standard online learning. The broader related-work coverage remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the main-text exposition, especially the setup, algorithmic-axis discussion, and Outlook. It reorganizes definitions, streamlines prose, changes notation, and introduces distinct theorem numbering with repaired references. Most retained appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Both experimental figures and both hyperparameter tables are deleted, while the notation table remains. Main-text mathematical displays and statement formatting are revised, producing substantial changes to the document's visual presentation beyond page renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves definition clarity, theorem navigation, and research positioning, but removes all empirical checks of Two-Gate. It also withdraws the empirical-validation claim and the Outlook comparison that was not reconciled with Figure 1. With the core proofs essentially unchanged, clearer exposition is traded against lost, imperfectly documented empirical support; the PDFs do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
